mechanism_narrative: A low level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced interest rates lower the discount rate for equity cash flows and increase corporate borrowing capacity.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day SPX returns remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 8.5% coupled with a monthly increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate earnings expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5% and UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) below 600k and unemployment (UNRATE) above 8.5% indicate severe economic contraction that triggers risk-off sentiment, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when HOUST < 600 and UNRATE > 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 signals supply chain disruptions that reduce corporate output and increase input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during supply shock regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 90.0.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST) above 650k indicate robust consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days in any economic regime.
failure_condition: Rank IC between HOUST and 5-day SPX returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year with a monthly increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals imminent monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (y/y) and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (y/y) and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with unemployment above 8.5% (UNRATE) signals aggressive monetary stimulus to counter economic weakness, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases when FEDFUNDS declines and UNRATE > 8.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.5% signals robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in strong growth regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 quarterly growth > 2.5%.
